title: At least three Antarctic sectors were below daily 1981-2010 ice extent 10th percentiles on all July-September 2023 days
abstract: At least three of five Antarctic sectors were below their 1981-2010 calendar-day ice extent 10th percentiles on all 92 days in July to September 2023. This full-winter result holds with two later reference periods. We use Sea Ice Index version 4 for 1979-2025. We extend earlier campaign joint-sign tests with daily tail events and year exclusion tests. The all-five below-mean event gives a null result under a sector-year shuffle, as in earlier work. The recent three-sector tail rate is 16.09 percent with a year-shuffle p value of 0.023. Without 2023, the rate is 6.76 percent and p is 0.254. The small unadjusted tail p values do not pass a correction for nine exploratory tests. These overlapping data do not give independent confirmation. Ten recent winters, fixed thresholds, trends, early satellite sampling and a 2025 sensor change limit inference. The analysis does not identify a physical cause or prove a change in coupling.
